C0.quote: classic Chamberlin-Courant multiwinner voting rule (CC) on single-peaked preference profiles
C0.note: Computational complexity of computing CC and Thiele winners.

C1.quote: We prove that CC is FPT with respect to d
C1.note: All main results are algorithms and lower bounds.

C2.1.value: preference profile; approval ballots; votes; misrepresentation function
C2.1.quote: A tuple (V, C, r) or (V, C, u) is called a preference profile

C2.2.quote: then we call a vote of v a weak order
C2.2.note: General misrepresentation functions are real-valued (CARD). Borda misrepresentation corresponds to linear orders. Approval ballots are also used.

C2.3.quote: measures how much a voter is misrepresented by a particular candidate
C2.3.note: Misrepresentation and utility functions are attributed to voters. The paper says balloting them fully is costly.

C2.4.quote: Balloting a misrepresentation function fully is costly for a voter
C2.4.note: The rule is applied directly to the misrepresentation function or preference profile. There is no statement about reporting or misreporting.

C4.1.quote: We can define it as: u(v, c) = maxc′ ∈C (r(v, c′ )) − r(v, c)
C4.1.note: Approval misrepresentation is defined as 0 iff approved and 1 otherwise. Thiele utility is defined as the sum of w_i over approved committee members.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: we define total utility of C ′ by u(C ′ )
C5.1.note: The problem definitions used in all results evaluate committees by total utility or total misrepresentation of voters.

C5.2.quote: we define total misrepresentation of C ′ by r(C ′ )
C5.2.note: Evaluation is on the input r or u, with no statement relating it to anything held separately.

VOT.quote_behav: a voter v gives an approval ballot as a vote
VOT.note: Voters' inputs are taken as given.
